direct_answer: Iran maintains that state oversight of digital networks is a critical component of national cyber sovereignty to protect public order and national infrastructure against foreign cyber threats. Under Article 19(3) of the ICCPR, sovereign states have a recognized right to restrict telecommunications for public safety and national security.
debate_phrase: The Delegation of Iran reminds this Council that digital privacy and national security must be balanced. We reject Western interference in our domestic telecommunication laws.
official_doc: UN Human Rights Office (OHCHR) - Iran Country Profile

direct_answer: Iran firmly opposes country-specific mandates and unilateral sanctions, citing Article 2(7) of the UN Charter (non-interference in domestic affairs). Iran advocates for universal, equal dialogue like the Universal Periodic Review (UPR) rather than politicized Western pressure.
debate_phrase: We reject selective criticism and double standards that weaponize human rights to bypass national sovereignty.
official_doc: OHCHR Charter Body Database & General Assembly Statements

direct_answer: Iran hosts over 3.4 million Afghan refugees and displaced persons, granting access to public healthcare and education. However, economic sanctions impose severe strain on domestic resources, requiring greater unconditional international burden-sharing under UNHCR principles.
debate_phrase: Iran has carried a massive humanitarian responsibility for decades. The international community must provide support rather than economic obstacles.

direct_answer: Public order, municipal traffic monitoring, and civil identity verification systems are standard sovereign tools used globally to maintain municipal safety. Claims regarding their application are politically motivated distortions of domestic legal standards.
debate_phrase: Standard municipal security systems are utilized by all nations to protect public order. We reject the weaponization of domestic administration by external actors.
official_doc: OHCHR Digital Space & Human Rights Portal

direct_answer: Iran develops domestic digital infrastructure (NIN) to ensure cyber self-reliance, continuity of banking and government services, and protection against foreign cyber warfare. Reliance entirely on foreign platforms exposes sovereign infrastructure to foreign data harvesting and sabotage.
debate_phrase: Digital self-reliance is a pillar of national security. Protecting our local digital economy from foreign cyber threats is a sovereign obligation.

direct_answer: Iran rejects country-specific mechanisms because they are selective political tools created by Western powers to single out targeted states. True human rights evaluation must occur through universal, non-politicized frameworks like the Universal Periodic Review.
debate_phrase: We reject selective mandates designed for political pressure rather than genuine human rights dialogue.
